- fixed statement
- providing legal actions in random order

- removed the board size line
- hopefully fixed the repetition detection

struct's old contribution: https://www.codingame.com/contribute/view/81076c184b40736253f4c9e4905ce43f33c6

- changed config to board size (it's constant, it's always 7, many other board games have it)

- added legal actions to the inputs; to discuss if keep it: theoretically they can rarely exceed 200 moves in holeless specific positions

Known issues: some issues with 3rd-fold repetition, sometimes it end prematurely.

Ataxx at least! Upvoted ! And kudos to struct too! You will please NNers.

Some remarks:
* IMHO, the config line is not needed. The board description is enough. I'd say the player id is convenient but you can guess it too from the first turn.
* On the statement: Jump: A player may jump from a cell to another cell that is two squares away in any direction(both vertically and horizontally). He can also jump two cells diagonally. The statement is wrong but the game mechanics are correct.
Changed to config to board size. I know it's constant, but many other board games have it.
Make it simpler. Remove the line

I've revised the statement as follows:
https://pastebin.com/MUxS3MrG

The differences between the original and revised versions can be found here:
https://pastebin.com/3zsXUebx

Please verify that my changes are correct, and update the statement with any necessary corrections.

I also have one question: the Input section states that [[lastAction]] may contain multiple actions separated by ";". Under what circumstances would multiple actions be provided? Or is that description redundant?

@darkhorse64: Would you mind taking a look at the revised statement as well and seeing if you have any comments or suggestions?

Thank you both.

It happens when one player has no moves (no free squares for spawn or jump in the neighborhood of their own pieces) but the board is not full. The opponent must be careful to fill the board with spawns until there is no space left . Using jump would leave holes that the stalemared player could use to resurrect from the grave.

Note that this situation is not necessarily a loss for the stalemated player because what matters is the number of own pawns when the game ends.

Thanks for the explanation.

I can understand that when one player is unable to move, the opponent may effectively get multiple consecutive actions. However, I was expecting [[lastAction]] to always contain exactly one action, so I was surprised to learn that this situation is treated as an exception and that multiple actions may be provided instead.

Update the statement, thank your for the work.
Player may pass if he's unable to move, like in Othello. But game is likely decided by then, but I left it for correctness.

My pleasure. I noticed a few changes that haven't been applied to the current version: Introduction * Game => The game (twice) * 7x7 => 7x7 board * Board => The board * or if => or Heading * "Legal action:" => "Legal actions" (plural and no colon). Input for one game turn * Next actionsCount lines: The tag should appear immediately after the word "lines" rather than at the end of the line. Thanks.
The updated statement looks good to me.

@jacek Thank you for fixing the statement.
@darkhorse64 Thank you for your review.
